title: After exchang alt and ctrl,  use alt + tab open the app switcher, when keep alt & tab down use left or right, ensue every keymap crash

fix_assessment.rationale: An observable failure is reported and a specific investigation boundary is identified. The proposed direction remains conditional on controlled reproduction.

steps: In a disposable profile configure the five exact screenshot mappings and use only test windows.
Invoke the app switcher through the mapped physical sequence, keep the same keys held and press each arrow; record physical versus logical key identities and invocation state.
Compare removing arrow mappings versus modifier swaps versus Ctrl+Tab mapping one at a time; distinguish hook loss, process exit and state-only failure.
prerequisites: Use a disposable test environment and test-owned documents/configuration; preserve existing user data.
reproduce.expected: Navigating the switcher should not disable subsequent remaps; each key-up must leave consistent state without requiring a secure-attention transition.

actions.label: Reproduce Keyboard Manager app switcher state behavior

evidence: The inspected screenshot contains LeftAlt to LeftCtrl, LeftCtrl to LeftAlt, Ctrl+Tab to Alt+Tab, Ctrl+Left to Home and Ctrl+Right to End.
The report says holding the switcher keys and pressing Left/Right dismisses the switcher and stops remapping; secure-attention entry then Escape restores it.
This is not evidence that the process crashes, and the extra arrow mappings in the screenshot are essential to reproduction.
judgment.rationale: The arrow-key remaps may interact with an already invoked Alt+Tab remap and swapped virtual/original modifier state. Isolate that exact combination and compare hook liveness with stuck invocation state before selecting a reset or key-up correction.
judgment.recommended_action: Execute the focused maintainer reproduction before choosing an implementation; the proposal is a hypothesis, not an approved detailed design.

verification: Navigating the switcher should not disable subsequent remaps; each key-up must leave consistent state without requiring a secure-attention transition.
Retest a matching unaffected control and the originally reported workflow on a current supported build.
